item.title: Sultanate Urges Muslims to Look Out for Rabi’ul Awwal Moon on Thursday
item.description:
The Sokoto Sultanate Council has called on Muslims across the country to look out for the new moon of Rabi’ul Awwal 1448 AH on Thursday, August 13, 2026.

The call was contained in a statement dated August 12 and signed by Prof. Sambo Wali Junaidu, Wazirin Sokoto and Chairman of the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council.

According to the council, Thursday, August 13, corresponds to 29 Safar 1448 AH and has therefore been designated as the day for Muslims to search for the new moon of Rabi’ul Awwal.

The council urged anyone who sights the moon to report it to the nearest District or Village Head, who will communicate the sighting to His Eminence Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, the Sultan of Sokoto and President-General of the Nigeria Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA).

Rabi’ul Awwal is an important month in the Islamic calendar. The 12th of Rabi’ul Awwal is traditionally observed by many Muslims as the birth date of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

Muslims in various communities, including followers of different Sufi orders, commonly mark the occasion through Maulud gatherings, religious lectures, Qur’anic recitations, praises and other Islamic activities.

The Sultanate Council prayed for Allah’s guidance and assistance for Muslims carrying out the religious duty of moon sighting and for a successful commencement of Rabi’ul Awwal 1448 AH.

item.title: Sultan Declares Thursday as First Day of Safar 1448AH in Nigeria
item.description:
The Sultan of Sokoto and President-General of the Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA), Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, has officially declared Thursday, July 16, 2026, as the first day of Safar 1448AH.

The announcement followed the inability of moon-sighting committees across Nigeria to confirm the sighting of the new Safar crescent on Tuesday, July 14, which corresponded to the 29th day of Muharram 1448AH.

In a statement issued by the Sultanate Council Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs and signed by its Chairman, Prof. Sambo Wali Junaidu, the council said no authenticated report of the crescent moon was received from any part of the country.

As a result, Wednesday, July 15, was declared the 30th and final day of Muharram 1448AH, completing the month in line with Islamic tradition.

Based on the report, the Sultan approved the commencement of the new Islamic month on Thursday, July 16, 2026.

The declaration serves as the official guide for Muslims across Nigeria in observing religious activities and events associated with the Islamic calendar.

item.title: Sultan of Sokoto Orders Nationwide Moon Sighting for Islamic New Year
item.description:
The Sultan of Sokoto and President-General of the Nigeria Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA), Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, has directed Muslims across Nigeria to observe the sighting of the new moon of Muharram, which marks the beginning of the Islamic New Year.

According to a statement from the Sultanate Council:

Monday, June 15, 2026 (29th day of Zulhijjah 1447AH) has been set for moon sighting

Muslims are encouraged to observe the sky after sunset

Any confirmed sightings should be reported through traditional channels

Reports are to be submitted to local district or village heads, who will forward them to the Sultanate Council for verification.

The annual moon sighting determines:

The start of Muharram, the first month of the Islamic calendar

The official beginning of the Islamic New Year in Nigeria

Timing of major religious observances throughout the year

Muharram is considered one of the sacred months in Islam and holds special spiritual significance for Muslims worldwide.


The Sultan’s announcement plays a key role in:

Ensuring nationwide uniformity in Islamic calendar observance

Promoting unity among Muslim communities

Guiding official religious declarations in the country

The Sultanate Council is expected to announce the official start of Muharram 1448AH after reviewing verified reports from across Nigeria.

Muslims across Nigeria have been urged to participate in the traditional moon sighting exercise, which will determine the beginning of the Islamic New Year and guide religious observances for the coming year.

item.title: Arafat Day to Hold May 26 as Saudi Declares Dhul Hijjah Begins
item.description:
Saudi Arabia has officially announced Tuesday, May 26, 2026, as the Day of Arafat and Wednesday, May 27, 2026, as Eid-el-Adha celebration day following the sighting of the Dhul Hijjah crescent moon.

The Saudi Supreme Court confirmed that Monday, May 18, marks the first day of Dhul Hijjah 1447 AH after receiving verified moon sighting reports from witnesses across the kingdom.

According to the court, the Day of Arafat — regarded as the peak of the annual Hajj pilgrimage — will be observed on May 26, while Muslims worldwide will celebrate Eid-el-Adha the next day.

The court also offered prayers for King Salman bin Abdulaziz and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for their continued service to pilgrims visiting the holy sites in Makkah and Madinah.

Saudi authorities further prayed for a peaceful and successful Hajj exercise and for the continued security and prosperity of the kingdom.

Haramain Info, the official account associated with the Two Holy Mosques, also confirmed the moon sighting on X, stating that Eid-el-Adha will be celebrated on Wednesday, May 27, Insha Allah.

Meanwhile, in Nigeria, the Sultan of Sokoto and President-General of the Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, earlier declared Monday, May 18, 2026, as the first day of Dhul Hijjah.

Dhul Hijjah is the twelfth and final month of the Islamic calendar and is considered one of the holiest periods in Islam. The month features major spiritual activities including Hajj, the Day of Arafat, and Eid-el-Adha celebrations observed by Muslims around the world.

item.title: Mafi karancin sadaki 2024
item.description:
Mafi karancin Sadakin aure a halin yanzu a shine N120,061 Kamar yadda kwamitin Duban wata na fadar sarkin musulmi a Najeriya ya sanar a shafinsa na X (twitter).

Sadaki adadin kudi ne da namiji ke bayarwa ga macen da zai aura don nuna ikhlasi da jajircewarsa ga aure wanda kuma ke nuna ma'anar nauyi da wajibci akan Shi, kuma wajibi ne mutum ya bayar da Sasakin ko kafin daura auren ko lokacin daura auren Ko kuma a matsayin bashi ya biya bayan an daura auren.

Article Translation in English Language:

The minimum dowry is currently N120,061 as announced by the Moon sight Committee of the Palace of the sultan of sokoto in Nigeria on its page X (twitter).

Dowry is the amount of money that a man gives to the woman he will marry to show his sincerity and commitment to marriage, which also shows the sense of responsibility and obligation on him, and it is obligatory for a person to give the Dowry either before or during the marriage. 
and as a debt he has to pay after the marriage.
